sam: Quick heads-up  rolled mini-batcher + adaptive-quant thresholds to canary. Short summary: p50 -11%, p95 -19%, projected infra token cost -28% on conv-tuned workload. :sparkles:

elena: Nice! What does "mini-batcher" do here?

sam: It groups many tiny chat requests into micro-batches earlier in the pipeline (pre-encode) and reshapes them into optimized decode slices. Less RPC overhead, fewer small GEMM calls. Works with new adaptive-quant to favor int8 paths when calibration looks safe.

dan: Canary numbers?

deploy-bot: Canary report (mini-q-2027-01-27): requests=110k, mix chat/completion 70/30, median seq 40, p50 43ms -> 38ms, p95 225ms -> 183ms, error rate stable 0.03% -> 0.03%. Dash: https://internal.redwood/perf/mini-q-2027-01-27

mike: Any signal on quality drift with adaptive quant?

sam: We ran quality hooks: embedding drift <0.4% and top-token agreement >99.6 for short convo cohort. We enforce a per-model quant-threshold and auto-fallback to float if mismatch >0.7.

elena: Host impact or regressions?

sam: Minor CPU increase on batching coordinator (~4%); we added a soft cap on concurrent micro-batches to avoid headroom exhaustion. No customer-facing regressions in canary.

eng-sre: Rollout plan added to runbook: canary -> 5% -> 30% (8h) -> 100% (36h). Auto-rollback triggers: p95 increase >5% OR error rate delta >0.15% OR quality hook fail.

cost-bot: If sustained, projected monthly infra token spend down ~26-31% for convo tiers (ref COST-2027-01-MINIQ).

sam: I'll post the config + short how-it-works in #docs and draft a 1-slide blurb for all-hands. Closing thread  will update after 30% step.
